title: Resilience Handshake: SLI Ownership Timeline & Oncall Commitment
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
We need a lightweight, repeatable 'handshake' process that captures SLI ownership transitions between Product, Engineering, and Oncall for every reliability initiative that consumes error budget. The goal is to reduce ambiguity during rollouts and ops handoffs by producing a timeline artifact (what, who, when), recording the oncall commitment windows, and surfacing it in the Reliability Initiative Hub dashboard. Deliverables: 1) a SLI Ownership Timeline template stored in Drive + Confluence how-to, 2) a tiny webhook that attaches the timeline artifact to initiative cards in the Initiative Hub, 3) a short oncall checklist and fallback policy for error-budget breaches (canary -> scale -> rollback), and 4) a short training doc for PMs and Eng leads. Success measured by: 80% of planned reliability rollouts include a completed timeline before canary; oncall acknowledges assignment in Slack thread; at least two teams use the process in Cycle 47.

Scope exclusions: deep automation of error-budget allocation (handled by separate PM ticket), and infra autoscaling policy changes (engineering work tracked separately). This ticket coordinates process, templates, visibility and the minimal integration to attach timeline artifacts to Initiative Hub cards.
acceptance_criteria: Ownership timeline template in Confluence + canonical copy in Drive (link in comments)
Initiative Hub shows the timeline URL in the initiative card metadata for new reliability initiatives
Oncall checklist and fallback policy doc published and linked from the timeline
Two pilot teams complete the timeline and confirm oncall acknowledgement during Cycle 47
Post-pilot feedback collected and at least three improvements logged as follow-up tickets
comments: 2025-11-12 - Aisha Raman: Initial draft of scope and acceptance criteria. Raised at Reliability Sync; Eng and Oncall SMs asked for minimal friction. Confluence stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/SLI+Ownership+Timeline (draft)

2025-11-14 - Jordan Lee: Spoke with Oncall leads (Maya Chen, Luis Ortega). They want two clear fields: 'Acknowledged by Oncall' (slack thread link) and 'Coverage window' (dates). Suggested including runbook link and escalation contact.

2025-11-19 - Maya Chen (Oncall): Added runbook checklist items. Recommended default fallback: degrade model variant -> increase dedicated pool by burst -> rollback. Will validate with PagerDuty playbook.

2025-11-22 - Eng review (Tom Alvarez): Technical constraint: Initiative Hub metadata has a 2KB limit; timeline must be stored in Drive and only URL attached. I'll add a small webhook that writes the Drive URL to initiative metadata. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/initiative-hub/pull/412

2025-11-25 - PM review (Renee Park): Suggested we require 'pre-canary' completion before canary gates trigger in the release playbook. Will coordinate with Release Manager. Logged follow-up ticket PM-33480 for gate enforcement automation.
2025-11-28 - Jordan Lee: Prototype timeline template uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleTimeline. Sharing set to org. Added short form for low-touch initiatives.

2025-12-01 - Pilot kickoff: Teams A and B onboarded. Team A filled timeline and acknowledged Oncall in Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CA1EXAMPLE/p1700000000. Team B requested a simplified template for hotfixes (created variant 'timeline-lite').

2025-12-02 - Aisha Raman: Consolidated pilot feedback. Three improvement items captured: 1) 'timeline-lite' formalized (PM-33485), 2) webhook should validate Drive link format (ENG-33490), 3) add a checkbox in Initiative Hub UI for 'Oncall acknowledged' (DES-33499). Moving this ticket to In Progress for integration work.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keep timeline human-editable to avoid brittle tooling. Aim for simple integration rather than embedding structured SLI data into the Initiative Hub metadata. If later we need structured queries, we'll introduce a small schema service (separate ticket).
UX decision: two templates (full + lite) to cover standard rollouts and emergency hotfixes. Lite template requires acknowledgement but fewer fields.
Operational decision: Oncall must acknowledge within 48 hours before canary; if not acknowledged, release manager will escalate per runbook.
